---
url: https://axios-cache-interceptor.js.org/guide.md
---
# Introduction

Axios Cache Interceptor is an axios interceptor that caches responses. It lets you call axios
as often as you need without overloading the network or writing your own error-prone cache.

Every request made through your axios instance passes through the interceptor, which decides
whether to send it to the network or answer it with a cached response.

## How it works

Axios runs interceptors before calling the adapter and again before returning the response
to the caller. The adapter is the last step and performs the actual network call. Because
this library is built on interceptors instead of a custom adapter, you can keep using any
axios adapter you want.

Before a request reaches the adapter, the request interceptor checks, among other
conditions:

* whether a valid cached response already exists;
* whether the request should be cached at all (sometimes you don't want caching, and that's
  fine);
* whether an identical request is already in flight, so this one can wait for its result.

After the adapter returns a response, the response interceptor checks whether it belongs to
a *cacheable* request, saves it to storage, resolves other requests waiting for the same
resource and returns the response to the original caller.

## Features

* TTL, `Cache-Control`, `ETag`, `Last-Modified` and `Vary` support.
* Returns the previous cached response when a new request fails.
* Deduplicates concurrent requests for the same resource.
* Configurable globally and per request.
* Built-in in-memory, `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` storages.
* Production UMD bundle of about 18 KiB minified (about 7 KiB gzipped), dependencies included.
* A development build that logs why each request was or wasn't cached.
* In a 2023 benchmark with cached responses, served about 21x more requests per second than
  plain axios and about 9% more than `axios-cache-adapter`.

## Alternatives

### axios-cache-adapter

This library was heavily inspired by axios-cache-adapter. That library was good, but it is
now unmaintained and has many unresolved issues. It is also larger than this library, with
fewer features and lower performance.

### Fetch with a state management library

This library was built specifically for axios and manages its own storage, request
deduplication and HTTP caching headers, which hand-rolled caches rarely cover. For state
management libraries and similar tools,
[this blog post](https://arthur.place/implications-of-cache-or-state) explains why a cache is
a better architectural fit than state.

# Getting started

[Looking for axios v0?](https://axios-cache-interceptor.js.org/v0/)

## Install

Install Axios and Axios Cache Interceptor:

::: code-group

```bash [NPM]
npm install axios@^1 axios-cache-interceptor@^1
```

```html [Browser]
<!-- Development UMD build (~22 KiB) -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/axios-cache-interceptor@1/dev/index.bundle.js"></script>

<!-- Production UMD build (~18 KiB) -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/axios-cache-interceptor@1/dist/index.bundle.js"></script>
```

```ts [Skypack]
import Axios from 'https://cdn.skypack.dev/axios';
import { setupCache } from 'https://cdn.skypack.dev/axios-cache-interceptor';
```

:::

## Setup

Import `setupCache` and apply it to your axios instance:

::: code-group

```ts [ECMAScript]
import Axios from 'axios';
import { setupCache } from 'axios-cache-interceptor';

const instance = Axios.create(); // [!code focus]
const axios = setupCache(instance); // [!code focus]

const req1 = axios.get('https://api.example.com/'); // [!code focus]
const req2 = axios.get('https://api.example.com/'); // [!code focus]

const [res1, res2] = await Promise.all([req1, req2]);

res1.cached; // false // [!code focus]
res2.cached; // true // [!code focus]
```

```ts [CommonJS]
const Axios = require('axios');
const { setupCache } = require('axios-cache-interceptor');

const instance = Axios.create(); // [!code focus]
const axios = setupCache(instance); // [!code focus]

const req1 = axios.get('https://api.example.com/'); // [!code focus]
const req2 = axios.get('https://api.example.com/'); // [!code focus]

const [res1, res2] = await Promise.all([req1, req2]);

res1.cached; // false // [!code focus]
res2.cached; // true // [!code focus]
```

```ts [Browser]
const Axios = window.axios;
const { setupCache } = window.AxiosCacheInterceptor;

const instance = Axios.create(); // [!code focus]
const axios = setupCache(instance); // [!code focus]

const req1 = axios.get('https://api.example.com/'); // [!code focus]
const req2 = axios.get('https://api.example.com/'); // [!code focus]

const [res1, res2] = await Promise.all([req1, req2]);

res1.cached; // false // [!code focus]
res2.cached; // true // [!code focus]
```

```ts [Skypack]
import Axios from 'https://cdn.skypack.dev/axios';
import { setupCache } from 'https://cdn.skypack.dev/axios-cache-interceptor';

const instance = Axios.create(); // [!code focus]
const axios = setupCache(instance); // [!code focus]

const req1 = axios.get('https://api.example.com/'); // [!code focus]
const req2 = axios.get('https://api.example.com/'); // [!code focus]

const [res1, res2] = await Promise.all([req1, req2]);

res1.cached; // false // [!code focus]
res2.cached; // true // [!code focus]
```

:::

`setupCache(instance)` registers both cache interceptors. If you need a custom interceptor
order, see [Other interceptors](./interceptors.md).

This is enough for most use cases. To change the defaults, pass a
[configuration object](../config.md) to `setupCache`. To change the behavior of a single
request, use the [`cache` option](../config/request-specifics.md#cache) in its request
config.

## Support table

Most breaking changes in Axios v0 were typing issues, so your version may work with a
combination outside this table. **Axios and Axios Cache Interceptor v0 are not compatible
with Axios and Axios Cache Interceptor v1.**

> **Note**: Not every v0 release declared Axios as a `peerDependency`, because Axios did not
> follow stable semver at the time.
> [See #145 (Comment)](https://github.com/arthurfiorette/axios-cache-interceptor/issues/145#issuecomment-1042710481)

| [Axios](https://github.com/axios/axios/releases) | [Axios Cache Interceptor](https://github.com/arthurfiorette/axios-cache-interceptor/releases) |
| ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `>= v1.7.8`                                      | `>= v1.7.0`                                                                                   |
| `>= v1.6`                                        | `>= v1.3.0 && <= 1.6.2`                                                                       |
| `>= v1.4`                                        | `>= v1.2.0`                                                                                   |
| `>= v1.3.1`                                      | `>= v1`                                                                                       |
| `>= v0.27`                                       | `>= v0.10.3`                                                                                  |
| `>= v0.26`                                       | `>= v0.8.4`                                                                                   |
| `~ v0.25`                                        | `~ v0.8.4`                                                                                    |
| `~ v0.24`                                        | `>= v0.5 && <= 0.8.3`                                                                         |
| `~ v0.23`                                        | `~ v0.4`                                                                                      |
| `~ v0.22`                                        | `~ v0.3`                                                                                      |
| `v0.21`                                          | `<= v0.2`                                                                                     |

# Debugging

When the cache does not behave as you expect, switch to the development build. It logs the
decisions the interceptors make, and why, through the [`debug`](../config.md#debug) option.

To use it, import `setupCache` from `/dev` and pass a `debug` function:

::: code-group

```ts [ECMAScript]
import Axios from 'axios';

// Import `setupCache` from `/dev`.
import { setupCache } from 'axios-cache-interceptor'; // [!code --]
import { setupCache } from 'axios-cache-interceptor/dev'; // [!code ++]

// Same API as the production build.
const axios = setupCache(Axios, {
  debug: console.log // [!code ++]
});
```

```ts [CommonJS]
const Axios = require('axios');

// Import `setupCache` from `/dev`.
const { setupCache } = require('axios-cache-interceptor'); // [!code --]
const { setupCache } = require('axios-cache-interceptor/dev'); // [!code ++]

// Same API as the production build.
const axios = setupCache(Axios, {
  debug: console.log // [!code ++]
});
```

```ts{3,4} [Browser]
const Axios = window.axios;

// Load the development bundle (dev/index.bundle.js) instead of dist. // [!code ++]
const { setupCache } = window.AxiosCacheInterceptor;

// Same API as the production build.
const axios = setupCache(Axios, {
  debug: console.log // [!code ++]
});
```

```ts {5,9} [Skypack]
import Axios from 'https://cdn.skypack.dev/axios';

// Import `setupCache` from `/dev`.
import { setupCache } from 'https://cdn.skypack.dev/axios-cache-interceptor'; // [!code --]
import { setupCache } from 'https://cdn.skypack.dev/axios-cache-interceptor/dev'; // [!code ++]

// Same API as the production build.
const axios = setupCache(Axios, {
  debug: console.log // [!code ++]
});
```

:::

The logs cover cache hits and misses, concurrent request deduplication, header
interpretation, `Vary` mismatches, error handling and more, depending on your configuration.
The development build also logs a message with `console.error` when it loads, as a reminder
not to ship it to production.

::: details Sample of logs for two concurrent requests followed by a third one.

```json
[
  // First request reaches the network
  {
    "id": "-644704205",
    "msg": "Making network request",
    "data": { "overrideCache": false, "cacheState": "empty" }
  },
  // Second request waits for the first one
  {
    "id": "-644704205",
    "msg": "Concurrent request found, reusing result"
  },
  {
    "id": "-644704205",
    "msg": "Concurrent request detected, waiting..."
  },
  // First request's response arrives
  {
    "id": "-644704205",
    "msg": "Caching response",
    "data": { "ttl": 300000, "interpretHeader": true }
  },
  {
    "id": "-644704205",
    "msg": "Found waiting deferred(s) and resolve them"
  },
  {
    "id": "-644704205",
    "msg": "Response cached successfully",
    "data": { "state": "cached", "ttl": 300000 }
  },
  // Second request reuses the cached response
  {
    "id": "-644704205",
    "msg": "Using cached response"
  },
  {
    "id": "-644704205",
    "msg": "Returned cached response"
  },

  // A third request, made later, is answered from the cache
  {
    "id": "-644704205",
    "msg": "Using cached response"
  },
  {
    "id": "-644704205",
    "msg": "Returned cached response"
  }
]
```

:::

# Storages

A storage adapter connects the cache interceptor to an in-memory or persistent data store.
It saves and retrieves cache entries and serializes them when the underlying store requires
it. You can use a built-in adapter, create your own, or install one published on npm.

The interceptors call the storage automatically. You can also reach the configured storage
through `axios.storage` to inspect or invalidate entries manually.

The library includes these storages:

* [Memory storage](#memory-storage), created with `buildMemoryStorage` (Node.js and web)
* [Web Storage API](#web-storage-api), created with `buildWebStorage` (web only)

## Concurrent requests

Concurrent request deduplication is local to each axios instance. While an eligible request
is tracked in the instance's in-memory waiting map, later requests for the same key wait for
its result instead of reaching the network. Overrides and Vary mismatches can still produce
additional requests.

A shared storage, such as Redis, shares completed cache entries but not the in-memory
waiting map. If two processes request the same uncached key at the same time, both may send
a network request. This is supported: each response completes normally, local waiting
requests are settled, and they either read the shared result or retry if no result is
available. The library does not provide a distributed lock or guarantee a single network
request across processes.

Duplicate requests are normally harmless for the default `GET` and `HEAD` methods. If you
enable caching for non-idempotent methods, you are responsible for making duplicate network
requests safe.

## Memory storage

::: tip

This is the default storage.

:::

Memory storage works in Node.js and browsers. Its entries are lost when the page reloads or
the process exits.

By default, responses and cached entries share object references. Mutating a response can
therefore mutate its cached value. Set `cloneData` to `true` to clone values returned by
`get()`, or use `'double'` to clone values on both `set()` and `get()`. See
[#163](https://github.com/arthurfiorette/axios-cache-interceptor/issues/163) and similar
reports.

For long-running processes, use `cleanupInterval`, `maxEntries`, and `maxStaleAge` to bound
memory usage and remove old entries.

The storage keeps entries in a JavaScript `Map`, exposed as `storage.data`.

```ts
import axios from 'axios';
import {
  setupCache,
  buildMemoryStorage
} from 'axios-cache-interceptor';

setupCache(axios, {
  // Memory storage is already the default.
  storage: buildMemoryStorage(
    /* cloneData default=*/ false,
    /* cleanupInterval default=*/ 5 * 60 * 1000,
    /* maxEntries default=*/ 1024,
    /* maxStaleAge default=*/ 60 * 60 * 1000
  )
});
```

Options:

* `cloneData`: clones values returned by `get()` when set to `true`. Use `'double'` to also
  clone values before saving them. The default is `false`.

* `cleanupInterval`: how often, in milliseconds, to remove old entries. Set it to `false` to
  disable automatic cleanup. The default is 5 minutes (`300_000`).

* `maxEntries`: the maximum number of entries to keep. Entry sizes cannot be measured
  reliably, so when the limit is reached the storage first removes entries that can be
  discarded (empty, must-revalidate, expired, or stale with a TTL beyond `maxStaleAge`),
  then evicts by state (empty, must-revalidate, stale, cached and finally loading), oldest
  first. Set it to `false` to disable the limit. The default is `1024`.

* `maxStaleAge`: how long, in milliseconds, a stale entry with a defined TTL can remain
  after expiring before it is removed. The default is 1 hour (`3_600_000`).

## Web Storage API

Use `buildWebStorage` to keep cached entries across page reloads. It stores entries as JSON
in the browser's
[Storage API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Storage).

::: code-group

```ts{7} [Local Storage]
import axios from 'axios';
import { setupCache, buildWebStorage } from 'axios-cache-interceptor';

setupCache(axios, { // [!code focus:5]
  // localStorage is shared with other code on the page, so
  // prefix all keys to avoid collisions.
  storage: buildWebStorage(localStorage, 'axios-cache:')
});
```

```ts{7} [Session Storage]
import axios from 'axios';
import { setupCache, buildWebStorage } from 'axios-cache-interceptor';

setupCache(axios, { // [!code focus:5]
  // sessionStorage is shared with other code on the page, so
  // prefix all keys to avoid collisions.
  storage: buildWebStorage(sessionStorage, 'axios-cache:')
});
```

```ts{5,8} [Custom Storage]
import axios from 'axios';
import { setupCache, buildWebStorage } from 'axios-cache-interceptor';

// Any object implementing the Storage interface // [!code focus:10]
const myStorage = createMyStorage();

setupCache(axios, {
  storage: buildWebStorage(
    myStorage,
    'axios-cache:', // prefix
    60 * 60 * 1000  // maxStaleAge (1 hour default)
  )
});
```

:::

Options:

* `storage`: the `Storage` instance to use, such as `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`.
* `prefix`: a prefix added to every key to avoid collisions. The default is
  `'axios-cache-'`.
* `maxStaleAge`: how long, in milliseconds, a stale entry with a defined TTL can remain
  after expiring before it is removed. The default is 1 hour (`3_600_000`).

### Browser quota

Since `v0.9.0`, the web storage evicts older entries when the browser's storage quota is
reached.

The storage handles quota errors as follows:

1. Try to save the value.
2. If the quota is exceeded, remove expired entries that cannot become stale.
3. Retry the write. If it still fails, remove the oldest entry with the configured prefix.
4. Repeat until the write succeeds or no matching entries remain.
5. If the write still fails, leave the new value unstored. The value itself may exceed the
   available quota, or another application may be using the remaining capacity.

## buildStorage()

All built-in storage adapters use `buildStorage`, and `setupCache` only accepts storages
created by it. Use the same function to create a custom adapter from the following methods:

* `set(key: string, value: NotEmptyStorageValue, currentRequest?: CacheRequestConfig): MaybePromise<void>`:
  saves a cache value under the given key.

* `remove(key: string, currentRequest?: CacheRequestConfig): MaybePromise<void>`: removes
  the value stored under the given key.

* `find(key: string, currentRequest?: CacheRequestConfig): MaybePromise<StorageValue | undefined>`:
  returns the stored value, or `undefined` when the key does not exist.

* `clear?(): MaybePromise<void>`: optionally clears all stored data. The interceptor does
  not call this method; it is available for application-level invalidation.

`find` only needs to return what was saved. The storage returned by `buildStorage` checks
expiration itself, turning expired entries into stale ones or removing them.

## Third-party storages

The following examples are not maintained as separate packages. Use them as starting points
and adapt their expiration and serialization behavior to your application.

* [Node Redis v4](#node-redis-storage)
* [IndexedDB](#indexeddb)
* [Node Cache](#node-cache)
* [Open a pull request](https://github.com/arthurfiorette/axios-cache-interceptor/pulls) to
  add another example.

## Node Redis storage

This example uses the Node Redis v4 client. The `PXAT` option gives every entry an absolute
expiration time, including temporary `loading` entries left behind by interrupted requests.

The expiration of a `loading` entry is only cleanup for abandoned requests. It does not
provide distributed request deduplication; multiple processes can still send the same
uncached request concurrently.

```ts
import { createClient } from 'redis';
import {
  buildStorage,
  canStale,
  type CacheRequestConfig,
  type NotEmptyStorageValue,
  type StorageValue
} from 'axios-cache-interceptor';

const client = createClient(/* connection config */);
await client.connect();

function getExpiresAt(
  value: NotEmptyStorageValue,
  request?: CacheRequestConfig
) {
  switch (value.state) {
    case 'loading': {
      // Abandoned loading entries must not remain forever.
      const requestTtl =
        request?.cache && typeof request.cache.ttl === 'number'
          ? request.cache.ttl
          : 60_000;

      return Date.now() + requestTtl;
    }

    case 'stale':
      if (value.ttl) {
        return value.createdAt + value.ttl;
      }

      break;

    case 'cached': {
      // Keep entries that can become stale long enough to be revalidated.
      const staleFor = Math.max(
        value.staleTtl ?? 0,
        canStale(value) ? 60 * 60 * 1000 : 0
      );

      return value.createdAt + value.ttl + staleFor;
    }
  }

  // Keep stale entries without a TTL for at most one hour.
  return Date.now() + 60 * 60 * 1000;
}

const redisStorage = buildStorage({
  async find(key) {
    const result = await client.get(`axios-cache-${key}`);
    return result ? (JSON.parse(result) as StorageValue) : undefined;
  },

  async set(key, value, request) {
    await client.set(`axios-cache-${key}`, JSON.stringify(value), {
      PXAT: getExpiresAt(value, request)
    });
  },

  async remove(key) {
    await client.del(`axios-cache-${key}`);
  }
});
```

You can use [`buildStorage`](#buildstorage) to integrate other systems such as localForage,
ioredis, or Memcached.

## IndexedDB

This example uses `idb-keyval` to store cache entries in IndexedDB.

```ts
import { buildStorage } from 'axios-cache-interceptor';
import { del, get, set } from 'idb-keyval';

const indexedDbStorage = buildStorage({
  async find(key) {
    const value = await get(key);

    if (!value) {
      return;
    }

    return JSON.parse(value);
  },

  async set(key, value) {
    await set(key, JSON.stringify(value));
  },

  async remove(key) {
    await del(key);
  }
});
```

## Node Cache

This example uses [node-cache](https://github.com/node-cache/node-cache). Check the package's
current maintenance status before using it in a new application.

```ts
import { buildStorage } from 'axios-cache-interceptor';
import NodeCache from 'node-cache';

const cache = new NodeCache({ stdTTL: 60 * 60 * 24 * 7 });

const cacheStorage = buildStorage({
  find(key) {
    return cache.get(key);
  },

  set(key, value) {
    cache.set(key, value);
  },

  remove(key) {
    cache.del(key);
  }
});
```

url: https://axios-cache-interceptor.js.org/guide/request-id.md
---
# Request ID

Every request has an `id` that tells it apart from other requests. The ID is the key used
to store its cache entry.

The ID binds a cache entry to its request, so you can reference or invalidate it later, and
it lets requests to the same endpoint with the same parameters share one cache entry.

The default ID generator ignores leading and trailing slashes, so
`{ baseURL: 'https://a.com/', url: '/b' }` and `{ url: 'https://a.com/b/' }` get the same ID.

::: code-group

```ts [Different requests]
import Axios from 'axios';
import { setupCache } from 'axios-cache-interceptor';

const axios = setupCache(Axios);
// [!code focus:5]
// These requests go to different endpoints, but they share
// the same cache entry because both use the same ID.
const reqA = await axios.get('/a', { id: 'custom-id' });
const reqB = await axios.get('/b', { id: 'custom-id' });
```

```ts [Different contexts]
import Axios from 'axios';
import { setupCache } from 'axios-cache-interceptor';

const axios = setupCache(Axios);
// [!code focus:7]
// The same approach creates two separate cache entries for one endpoint,
// so each use case gets its own cache.
const userForPageX = await axios.get('/users', { id: 'users-page-x' });
const userForPageY = await axios.get('/users', { id: 'users-page-y' });
```

:::

::: warning

If you give two different requests the same ID, the library ignores any differences between
them and both share the same cache entry.

:::

## Custom generator

By default, the ID generator takes the request's `method`, `baseURL`, `url`, `params` and
`data` (plus, when [`Vary`](../config/request-specifics.md#cache-vary) requires it, the values
of the request headers it lists), and hashes them with [`object-code`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/object-code) into a 32-bit
number.

This is unique enough for most applications, but there is a
[theoretical 50% chance of a collision after about 77,000 keys](https://preshing.com/20110504/hash-collision-probabilities/).

With [`buildWebStorage`](./storages.md#web-storage-api), this limit rarely matters, because
the ~5 MB quota of `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` fills up long before that many
entries.

::: warning

If you may exceed 77,000 unique keys, write a custom key generator that uses a hash with a
lower collision probability, such as
[`object-hash`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/object-hash).

:::

Create a generator with `buildKeyGenerator`. The resulting generator still returns
`config.id` when it is set. If your function returns a string or number, it is used as the
key directly; any other value is hashed with `object-code`.

The second argument, `meta`, holds the request header values selected by `Vary`. Include it
in the key, otherwise requests that differ in those headers share the same cache entry.

This example only uses the `url`, `method`, a `custom` property and the `Vary` values:

```ts
import Axios from 'axios';
import { setupCache, buildKeyGenerator } from 'axios-cache-interceptor';

const axios = setupCache(Axios, {
  generateKey: buildKeyGenerator((request, meta /* [!code focus:6] */) => ({
    method: request.method,
    url: request.url,
    custom: logicWith(request.method, request.url),
    vary: meta?.vary
  }))
});
```

url: https://axios-cache-interceptor.js.org/guide/invalidating-cache.md
---
# Invalidating cache

With a cache-first approach, data inconsistency becomes your main problem. **You** can change
data on the server, and so can **others**. Without asking the server, there is no way to know
the current state of the data.

::: warning

**All revalidation methods below only run when the request succeeds.**

To revalidate after a non-`2XX` status code, accept that status in axios's
[`validateStatus`](https://axios-http.com/docs/handling_errors) or revalidate manually as
shown [below](#through-external-sources).

:::

Consider this example:

1. The user lists all posts, and the server returns an empty array.
2. The user creates a new post, and the server returns 200 OK.
3. Your frontend navigates back to the post list page.
4. The page still shows 0 posts, because the list request was recently cached.
5. Your client shows 0 posts, but the server has 1.

## Revalidation after mutation

Most of the time, your own client causes the inconsistency, as in the example above, where it
sent the mutation request itself. In that case, you can invalidate the cache of every entry
the mutation changed.

**The `cache.update` option is available on every request, and it is the main tool for
invalidation.**

::: tip

Wrapping each request in its own function makes it easier to keep track of the custom IDs
each request uses, and to reference and invalidate them later.

:::

## Programmatically

If the mutation made a simple change, you can use the mutation response to update your cache
directly.

In the example above, you only need to push the new post into the `list-posts` cache entry.

```ts
// Uses the `list-posts` ID so it can be referenced later.
function listPosts() {
  return axios.get('/posts', {
    id: 'list-posts'
  });
}

function createPost(data) {
  return axios.post(
    '/posts',
    data,
    /* [!code focus:25] */ {
      cache: {
        update: {
          // Updates the cache entry of the `list-posts` request.
          'list-posts': (listPostsCache, createPostResponse) => {
            // Nothing to update if the entry is not cached
            if (listPostsCache.state !== 'cached') {
              return 'ignore';
            }

            // Assume the `list-posts` response body is { posts: Post[] }
            // and the create post response body is the new post.

            // Adds the new post to the end of the cached list
            listPostsCache.data.data.posts.push(createPostResponse.data);

            // Returns the updated cache entry to be stored.
            return listPostsCache;
          }
        }
      }
    }
  );
}
```

This updates the `list-posts` cache on the client so it matches the server. When an update
like this is possible, prefer it, because it doesn't need another request to the server.

::: tip

**Note to Vue users:** with the default memory storage, the cached array is the same object
that the previous request returned. If you modify it as shown above and assign the response
data to a Vue `ref`, the UI may not update. Copy the array before modifying it:

```ts
const posts = listPostsCache.data.data.posts;

listPostsCache.data.data.posts = [...posts];
listPostsCache.data.data.posts.push(createPostResponse.data);
// or
listPostsCache.data.data.posts = [...posts, createPostResponse.data];
```

Or copy it before assigning it to the `ref`:

```ts
const response = await axios.get('/posts', { id: 'list-posts' });
myRef.value = [...response.data.posts];
```

You can also build the memory storage with `cloneData` enabled, so every read returns a copy.
See [Memory Storage](./storages.md#memory-storage).

:::

## Through network

Sometimes the mutation is complex enough that replicating every change the backend made would
duplicate a lot of service code and become hard to maintain.

In those cases, invalidate the cache and let the next request go to the server, which updates
the cache with the new response.

```ts
// Uses the `list-posts` ID so it can be referenced later.
function listPosts() {
  return axios.get('/posts', {
    // [!code focus:3]
    id: 'list-posts'
  });
}

function createPost(data) {
  return axios.post('/posts', data, {
    // [!code focus:9]
    cache: {
      update: {
        // Calls storage.remove('list-posts') internally, so the
        // next request goes to the server without any extra
        // checks on your side.
        'list-posts': 'delete'
      }
    }
  });
}
```

In the first example, at step **3**, the axios-cache-interceptor instance requests the posts
from the server again and updates the cache before the promise resolves and your page renders.

## Through external sources

If you receive changes from somewhere else, such as a WebSocket listener, you may want to
update the axios cache outside of a request.

For that, use the storage directly:

```ts
if (someLogicThatShowsIfTheCacheShouldBeInvalidated) {
  // Deletes the cache entry of the `list-posts` request.
  await axios.storage.remove('list-posts');
}

if (someLogicThatShowsIfTheCacheShouldBeInvalidated) {
  // Deletes all cached data. `clear` is optional for custom storages.
  await axios.storage.clear?.();
}
```

## Keeping cache up to date

If someone else changed the data, your client may not know about it. In a chat application,
for example, your client may not know that someone sent you a new message.

When you have **no** way to know that the cache is outdated, set a shorter time to live (TTL)
for those requests.

```ts
// Uses the `list-posts` ID so it can be referenced later.
function listPosts() {
  return axios.get('/posts', {
    id: 'list-posts',
    cache: {
      ttl: 1000 * 60 // 1 minute.
    }
  });
}

function createPost(data) {
  return axios.post('/posts', data, {
    cache: {
      update: {
        // Still delete the cache when I KNOW things have changed.
        // Unless the server sends its own cache headers, the
        // cache is at most 1 minute out of date.
        'list-posts': 'delete'
      }
    }
  });
}
```

## Choosing a strategy

Any cache trades data consistency for performance, and most of the time that trade is worth
it.

*The best strategy usually combines several approaches: TTL, invalidation after mutations,
stale-while-revalidate and the others on this page.*

Weigh how much inconsistency you can accept against the performance you want to gain;
sometimes that means not caching at all.

---

---
url: https://axios-cache-interceptor.js.org/guide/interceptors.md
---
# Other interceptors

When you combine `axios-cache-interceptor` with other interceptors, the order in which they run
matters.

## Default order

`setupCache(axios)` registers both cache interceptors immediately, and axios runs the two kinds
of interceptors in different orders:

* Request interceptors run in **reverse order**: the last one added runs first (LIFO,
  *Last In, First Out*). Request interceptors registered before `setupCache()` run after the
  cache interceptor, and those registered after it run before it.
* Response interceptors run in **insertion order**: the first one added runs first (FIFO,
  *First In, First Out*). Response interceptors registered before `setupCache()` run before
  the cache interceptor, and those registered after it run after it.

See the [Axios documentation](https://github.com/axios/axios#interceptors) and
[this issue](https://github.com/arthurfiorette/axios-cache-interceptor/issues/449#issuecomment-1370327566)
for more details.

```ts
// Runs AFTER the cache interceptor
axios.interceptors.request.use((req) => req);

// Runs BEFORE the cache interceptor
axios.interceptors.response.use((res) => res);

setupCache(axios);

// Runs BEFORE the cache interceptor
axios.interceptors.request.use((req) => req);

// Runs AFTER the cache interceptor
axios.interceptors.response.use((res) => res);
```

## Custom order

For full control, disable automatic registration with `register: false` and register the
cache interceptors yourself.

```ts
import Axios from 'axios';
import { setupCache } from 'axios-cache-interceptor';

const axios = setupCache(Axios.create(), { register: false });

// Register the cache response interceptor first (response interceptors are FIFO)
axios.interceptors.response.use(
  axios.responseInterceptor.onFulfilled,
  axios.responseInterceptor.onRejected
);

// Register your own interceptors
axios.interceptors.request.use((req) => req);
axios.interceptors.response.use((res) => res);

// Register the cache request interceptor last (request interceptors are LIFO)
axios.interceptors.request.use(
  axios.requestInterceptor.onFulfilled,
  axios.requestInterceptor.onRejected
);
```

***

## Extending types

axios-cache-interceptor uses its own types instead of the default `AxiosInstance`,
`AxiosRequestConfig` and `AxiosResponse`. The library defines new interfaces instead of
augmenting axios's own, to avoid breaking other libraries that use axios.

As a result, when you integrate with other packages or write your own interceptor, you need
to extend our `AxiosCacheInstance`, `CacheRequestConfig` and `CacheAxiosResponse` types:

```ts
declare module 'axios-cache-interceptor' {
  interface CacheRequestConfig<R = any, D = any, P = any> {
    customProperty?: string;
  }
}
```

## Streams and non-JSON data

The cache stores `response.data` as it is. A stream can only be read once, so a cached stream
cannot be served again, and storages that serialize entries with `JSON.stringify`, such as
[`buildWebStorage`](./storages.md#web-storage-api), cannot keep buffers either.

To cache non-JSON responses in any storage, ask axios for a serializable type with
`responseType`, such as `'text'`, and use axios's native `transformResponse` option to turn
the data into a string or plain object. It receives the response data and must return the
transformed value synchronously:

```ts
import Axios from 'axios';
import { setupCache } from 'axios-cache-interceptor';

const instance = Axios.create();
const axios = setupCache(instance);
// [!code focus:8]
const response = await axios.get('my-url-that-returns-csv', {
  responseType: 'text',
  transformResponse(data) {
    // You will need to implement this function.
    return convertCsvToObject(data);
  }
});

response.data; // A plain object that can be cached.
```

`transformResponse` only runs for network responses. Cached responses already hold the
transformed data, so it is not applied again.

If you need `response.data` to stay a stream or a buffer, disable the cache for that request
and cache the data manually.

## Custom adapters

If you write a custom axios adapter, **always throw an `AxiosError`** (not a plain `Error` or
any other type) when the request fails. The cache interceptor reads `AxiosError.config` to
identify which in-flight request failed, so it can clean up its internal state (the
deferred in the waiting map and the loading cache entry).

If your adapter throws anything else, the interceptor cannot tell which request failed. The
cache entry stays in the `loading` state, and every later request for that key hangs
indefinitely. The development build logs a debug message when this happens.

```ts
import { AxiosError } from 'axios';

// Correct: always throw an AxiosError
const myAdapter = async (config) => {
  try {
    // ... perform request ...
  } catch (err) {
    throw new AxiosError(err.message, err.code, config);
  }
};

// Incorrect: plain errors bypass the cache error handler
const badAdapter = async (config) => {
  throw new TypeError('socket hang up'); // The cache state gets stuck!
};
```

---

---
url: https://axios-cache-interceptor.js.org/config.md
---
# setupCache()

`setupCache` receives an axios instance and the optional properties described below. It
modifies the instance in place and returns it. Call it only once per instance; a second call
throws an error.

```ts
const axios = setupCache(axiosInstance, OPTIONS);
```

::: tip

`setupCache` also accepts every `cache.*` [request-specific](./config/request-specifics.md)
option, passed at the top level (`{ ttl }`, not `{ cache: { ttl } }`). Values passed here
become the defaults for all requests made with this instance.

:::

::: warning

Calling `setupCache(Axios, OPTIONS)` on the default axios export only caches requests made
through that default instance. Instances created afterwards with `Axios.create()` do not get
the cache interceptors, and calling `setupCache` on them throws, because they inherit the
`defaults.cache` value set by the first call.

To share cached data between instances, call `setupCache` on each instance and pass them the
same [`storage`](#storage).

:::

## location

* Type: `InstanceLocation` (`'client' | 'server'`)
* Default: `typeof window === 'undefined' ? 'server' : 'client'`

A hint to the library about where the axios instance is running. The default header
interpreter uses it for `Cache-Control: private`. When the location is `'server'`, those
responses are not cached.

`setupCache` always detects this value and ignores any `location` passed in its options. To
change it, assign the property after setup:

```ts
const axios = setupCache(Axios.create());

// Treat this instance as a browser client, even when running in Node.js
axios.location = 'client';
```

## storage

* Type: `AxiosStorage`
* Default: `buildMemoryStorage()`

The storage saves, retrieves and, when needed, serializes the responses received from the
network.

See the [Storages](./guide/storages.md) page for more information.

## generateKey

* Type: `KeyGenerator<unknown, unknown>`
* Default: `defaultKeyGenerator`

The function that generates the cache key (the request ID) for each request.

The default generator returns the request's `id` when one is set. Otherwise, it hashes the
request's `method`, `baseURL`, `url`, `params` and `data` into a 32-bit key. When
[`Vary`](./config/request-specifics.md#cache-vary) requires it, the values of the request
headers it lists are included too.

::: warning

If a persistent cache may hold more than 77K unique keys, use a stronger hashing algorithm.

[Read more](./guide/request-id.md#custom-generator)

:::

## waiting

* Type: `Map<string, Deferred<void>>`
* Default: `new Map()`

A map holding a deferred promise for each pending request, used to deduplicate concurrent
requests.

You shouldn't change it. It is exposed in case you want to use it as a listener, for example
to know when a request is waiting for another one to finish.

## headerInterpreter

* Type: `HeaderInterpreter`
* Default: `defaultHeaderInterpreter`

The function that reads the response headers and determines the time to live (`ttl`) of the
cache entry. It receives the response headers and the instance's [`location`](#location).

The default interpreter handles `Cache-Control` (`no-cache`, `no-store`, `private`,
`immutable`, `max-age`, `max-stale` and `stale-while-revalidate`), `Age` and `Expires`.

::: warning

Many REST backends return some variation of `Cache-Control: no-cache` or
`Cache-Control: no-store`, which tells the library not to cache the response at all. Set
[`cache.interpretHeader`](./config/request-specifics.md#cache-interpretheader) to `false` for
those requests.

*If the debug mode prints `Cache-Control header indicates: do not cache`, this is probably
the reason.*

:::

The possible return values are:

* `'dont cache'`: the response will not be cached.
* `'not enough headers'`: the [`cache.ttl`](./config/request-specifics.md#cache-ttl) option
  is used instead.
* `number`: used as the TTL, in milliseconds.
* `{ cache: number, stale?: number }`: used as the TTL and the stale TTL, in milliseconds.

::: details Example of a custom headerInterpreter

```ts
import Axios from 'axios';
import {
  setupCache,
  type HeaderInterpreter
} from 'axios-cache-interceptor';

const myHeaderInterpreter: HeaderInterpreter = (headers) => {
  if (headers['x-my-custom-header']) {
    const seconds = Number(headers['x-my-custom-header']);

    if (seconds < 1) {
      return 'dont cache';
    }

    // The TTL is in milliseconds
    return seconds * 1000;
  }

  return 'not enough headers';
};

const axios = setupCache(Axios.create(), {
  headerInterpreter: myHeaderInterpreter
});
```

:::

## requestInterceptor

* Type: `AxiosInterceptor<InternalCacheRequestConfig<unknown, unknown>>`
* Default: `defaultRequestInterceptor(axios)`

The interceptor that runs before the request is sent to the axios adapter.

It is the main function of this library and connects the axios request to the cache.

It isn't meant to be replaced, but you can pass your own implementation to this property if
you need to.

See [its source code](https://github.com/arthurfiorette/axios-cache-interceptor/tree/main/src/interceptors)
for more information.

## responseInterceptor

* Type: `AxiosInterceptor<Partial<CacheAxiosResponse<unknown, unknown>> & AxiosResponse<unknown, unknown>>`
* Default: `defaultResponseInterceptor(axios)`

The interceptor that runs after the axios adapter returns a response.

It is the second most important function of this library and connects the axios response
to the cache.

It isn't meant to be replaced, but you can pass your own implementation to this property if
you need to.

See [its source code](https://github.com/arthurfiorette/axios-cache-interceptor/tree/main/src/interceptors)
for more information.

## register

* Type: `boolean`
* Default: `true`

Controls whether `setupCache()` registers the cache interceptors automatically.

* `true`: registers both cache interceptors (default).
* `false`: does not register them.

Use `false` when you need full control over the interceptor order. See
[Other interceptors](./guide/interceptors.md) for how axios orders interceptors.

```ts
import Axios from 'axios';
import { setupCache } from 'axios-cache-interceptor';

const axios = setupCache(Axios.create(), { register: false });

// Register the cache response interceptor first (response interceptors are FIFO)
axios.interceptors.response.use(
  axios.responseInterceptor.onFulfilled,
  axios.responseInterceptor.onRejected
);

// Register your own interceptors
axios.interceptors.request.use((req) => req);
axios.interceptors.response.use((res) => res);

// Register the cache request interceptor last (request interceptors are LIFO)
axios.interceptors.request.use(
  axios.requestInterceptor.onFulfilled,
  axios.requestInterceptor.onRejected
);
```

## debug

&#x20;

* Type: `(msg: { id?: string; msg?: string; data?: unknown }) => void` or `undefined`
* Default: `undefined` (no logging)

::: warning

This option only works with the [development build](./guide/debugging.md).

:::

A function that receives debug information about every caching decision. Use it to trace
unexpected behavior. It receives an object with optional `id`, `msg` and `data` fields, and
returns nothing.

Read the [Debugging](./guide/debugging.md) page for the complete guide.

::: details Example of a custom debug function

```ts
// Alternatives: pick one per instance.

// Prints debug info to the console.
setupCache(Axios.create(), { debug: console.log });

// Sends it to your own logging platform.
setupCache(Axios.create(), {
  debug: ({ id, msg, data }) =>
    myLoggerExample.emit({ id, msg, data })
});

// Disables debugging (default).
setupCache(Axios.create(), { debug: undefined });
```

:::

---

---
url: https://axios-cache-interceptor.js.org/config/request-specifics.md
---
# Request specifics

Each request can customize its caching through the `cache` property.

::: tip

Every request-specific property can also be passed to `setupCache`, the same way as the
[global options](../config.md), to change the default for all requests.

:::

## id

* Type: `string`
* Default: *(generated by the current
  [key generator](../guide/request-id.md#custom-generator))*

A custom [Request ID](../guide/request-id.md) for this request. When it is not set, the key
generator creates one from the request properties.

## cache

* Type: `Partial<CacheProperties<R, D>> | false`
* Default: `{}` *(inherits from the global configuration)*

::: tip

Any property you leave out inherits its value from the global configuration.

:::

The `cache` property is where all per-request cache customization happens. Pass an object
with the cache properties you want to change for this request.

To disable caching for a specific request, use `cache: { enabled: false }`. Disabling the
cache does not remove an existing entry from the storage:

```ts
// Make a request with cache disabled
const { id: requestId } = await axios.get('url', {
  cache: { enabled: false }
});

// Delete the cache entry for this request if needed
await axios.storage.remove(requestId);
```

`cache: false` still works for backward compatibility, but it will be removed in the next
major release. Use `cache: { enabled: false }` instead.

## cache.enabled

* Type: `boolean`
* Default: `true`

Whether the cache is enabled for this request. When set to `false`, the request skips the
cache entirely.

Set it to `false` globally and `true` per request for an **opt-in cache**.

### Example: opt-in cache

Disable the cache by default and enable it only for specific endpoints:

```ts
import { setupCache } from 'axios-cache-interceptor';

// Cache is disabled by default
const axios = setupCache(axiosInstance, {
  enabled: false
});

// Most requests won't use the cache
await axios.get('/api/realtime-data'); // Not cached

// Enable the cache for specific heavy or expensive requests
await axios.get('/api/heavy-computation', {
  cache: {
    enabled: true,
    ttl: 1000 * 60 * 10 // Cache for 10 minutes
  }
}); // Cached
```

### Example: opt-out cache

The cache is enabled by default and disabled for specific endpoints:

```ts
import { setupCache } from 'axios-cache-interceptor';

// Cache is enabled by default (you can omit this option)
const axios = setupCache(axiosInstance, {
  enabled: true
});

// Most requests use the cache
await axios.get('/api/user-profile'); // Cached

// Disable the cache for specific real-time endpoints
await axios.get('/api/live-stock-prices', {
  cache: { enabled: false }
}); // Not cached
```

## cache.ttl

* Type: `number | ((response: CacheAxiosResponse) => number | Promise<number>)`
* Default: `1000 * 60 * 5` *(5 minutes)*

::: warning

When [**interpretHeader**](#cache-interpretheader) is enabled, this value is only used when
the response headers don't determine a TTL.

:::

The time, in milliseconds, until the cached value expires.

If you pass a function, it receives the complete response and must return the TTL.

The `ttl` is only applied when the response is **first cached**; changing it on later
requests has no effect on the existing entry. See
[#1024](https://github.com/arthurfiorette/axios-cache-interceptor/issues/1024) for
workarounds.

## cache.interpretHeader

* Type: `boolean`
* Default: `true`

When enabled, the `ttl` is inferred from the response headers, following the MDN docs and
the HTTP specification. Responses with `Cache-Control: no-cache` or `no-store` are not cached.

See the
[`interpretHeader` implementation](https://github.com/arthurfiorette/axios-cache-interceptor/blob/main/src/header/interpreter.ts)
for more information.

## cache.cacheTakeover

* Type: `boolean`
* Default: `true`

Most of this library's caching depends on standard HTTP headers, and browsers use the same
headers for their own cache.

::: details You can see the browser cache in the network tab of your browser's dev tools.

![Network tab in Chrome DevTools](../assets/disk-cache-screenshot.png "A network disk-cache example")

:::

When your routes include `Cache-Control` in their responses, both the library and your
browser may cache the response, resulting in a **double layer of cache**.

This option adds headers to the request that tell any client or adapter not to cache the
response, so only the library caches it. Headers you already set on the request are not
overwritten.

**These headers are only added to this request and don't affect any other request or
response the server handles.**

Headers included:

* `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate, max-age=0`
* `Pragma: no-cache`
* `Expires: 0`

::: info Safari compatibility

The `max-age=0` directive is included for Safari (including iOS Safari), which has
historically cached more aggressively and may ignore `no-cache` on its own.

:::

::: tip Alternative

`cacheTakeover` works in most browsers, according to
[this StackOverflow answer](https://stackoverflow.com/a/2068407), but it may be unreliable in
rare cases because of browser-specific behavior or network intermediaries.

For maximum reliability, add a random query parameter instead:

```ts
axios.get(
  `/api/data?cachebuster=${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`,
  {
    id: 'api-data-endpoint' // Keeps the same cache key even though the URL changes
  }
);
```

Your backend can ignore the `cachebuster` value. This **guarantees** the browser won't cache
the response while axios-cache-interceptor keeps working as usual.

:::

::: warning CORS considerations

This option does not work for **CORS** requests when the server doesn't allow these headers.
The browser throws:
`Request header field Pragma is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Headers in preflight response.`

To fix it, add `Cache-Control`, `Pragma` and `Expires` to the `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`
of your server's CORS configuration.

If you cannot change the CORS configuration, you can:

1. Disable this option (`cacheTakeover: false`).
2. Use the query parameter approach described above.

Learn more about why this option is enabled by default in
[#437](https://github.com/arthurfiorette/axios-cache-interceptor/issues/437#issuecomment-1361262194)
and in this [StackOverflow answer](https://stackoverflow.com/a/2068407).

:::

## cache.methods

* Type: `Method[]`
* Default: `["get", "head"]`

The HTTP methods that should be cached. The default only caches `GET` and `HEAD`; use this
option to enable caching for `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE` and other methods.

To enable caching for `POST` requests:

```ts
// Enables caching for POST requests globally
const axios = setupCache(instance, {
  methods: ['get', 'post']
});

// Or just for this request
axios.post('url', data, {
  cache: {
    methods: ['post']
  }
});
```

`methods` is a per-request option because some requests are exceptions to the global rule.

## cache.cachePredicate

* Type: `CachePredicate<R, D>`
* Default:
  `{ statusCheck: (status) => [200, 203, 300, 301, 302, 404, 405, 410, 414, 501].includes(status) }`
  *(the cacheable status codes defined by RFC 7231)*

An object, or a function that receives the response, that decides whether a response can be
cached. The object form accepts:

* `statusCheck`: caches only if this function returns `true` for the response status.
* `containsHeaders`: caches only if every function returns `true` for its response header.
  Header names are lowercase in axios; a missing header calls the function with `undefined`.
* `responseMatch`: caches only if this function returns `true` for the response.
* `ignoreUrls`: never caches requests whose URL matches any of these patterns.
* `allowUrls`: only caches requests whose URL matches at least one of these patterns.

`ignoreUrls` and `allowUrls` are tested against `config.url` only (`baseURL` is not
included) before the request is sent. A string pattern matches when the URL contains it. If a
URL matches both lists, `ignoreUrls` takes precedence. When the request has no `url` (only a
`baseURL`), both lists are ignored.

```ts
axios.get<{ auth: { status: string } }>('url', {
  cache: {
    cachePredicate: {
      // Only cache if the response comes with a "good" status code
      statusCheck: (status) => true, // some calculation

      // Tests against any header present in the response
      containsHeaders: {
        'x-custom-header-3': (value) => true // some calculation
      },

      // Checks the response body
      responseMatch: ({ data }) => {
        // Only caches authenticated responses
        return data.auth.status === 'authenticated';
      },

      // Never caches requests whose URL starts with "/api"
      ignoreUrls: [/^\/api/],

      // Only caches requests whose URL includes "weekly"
      allowUrls: ['weekly']
    }
  }
});
```

## cache.update

* Type: `CacheUpdater<R, D>`
* Default: `{}`

When this request succeeds with a network response (not a cache hit), it updates or deletes
the cache entries of other requests. It is a `Record` keyed by request ID, where each value
is either:

* `'delete'`: removes that cache entry.
* a function that receives the current cache entry and this request's response, and returns
  the new cache entry, `'delete'` to remove it or `'ignore'` to leave it unchanged. Entries
  that are still loading are skipped.

You can also pass a single function instead of a record. It receives the response and can do
anything, but this is not recommended: it is simpler to consume the response normally and
write your own code after it.

```ts
// Request IDs used by other requests
let profileInfoId: string;
let userInfoId: string;

axios.post<{ auth: { user: User } }>(
  'login',
  { username, password },
  {
    cache: {
      update: {
        // The user is now authenticated, so the profile info must be fetched again
        [profileInfoId]: 'delete',

        // Writes the logged-in user into the cached user info response
        [userInfoId]: (cachedValue, response) => {
          if (cachedValue.state !== 'cached') {
            // Only update entries that are cached
            return 'ignore';
          }

          cachedValue.data.data = response.data.auth.user;

          // This value is stored and returned by later requests to this cache entry
          return cachedValue;
        }
      }
    }
  }
);
```

See [Invalidating cache](../guide/invalidating-cache.md) for more examples.

## cache.etag

* Type: `string | boolean`
* Default: `true`

Configures [`ETag`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/ETag) and
[`If-None-Match`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/If-None-Match)
handling for cache revalidation.

* `true`: stores the response's `ETag` and sends it in `If-None-Match` when revalidating a
  stale entry.
* `string`: sends this static value in `If-None-Match` instead.
* `false`: disables `ETag` handling.

A cached entry with an `ETag` becomes stale instead of being removed when its TTL expires. A
`304 Not Modified` response reuses the stored data and refreshes the entry.

## cache.modifiedSince

* Type: `Date | boolean`
* Default: `false` *(`true` when `etag: false` is passed to `setupCache`)*

Sends the
[`If-Modified-Since`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/If-Modified-Since)
header when revalidating a stale entry. Use a `Date` to send a custom static value, or `true`
to derive it from the cached response.

If the request was never cached before, the header is not set.

With `true`, the value of the response's
[`Last-Modified`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Last-Modified)
header is used when present; otherwise, the cache creation timestamp is sent.

## cache.staleIfError

* Type: `number | boolean | StaleIfErrorPredicate<R, D>`
* Default: `true`

When a request that revalidates a stale cache entry fails, the library returns the stale data
instead of the error. This covers network errors, rejected status codes and similar failures. The
returned response has `cached: true` and `stale: true`.

* `true`: returns the stale data. If the error response has a
  `Cache-Control: stale-if-error=N` header, only within `N` seconds after the entry was
  cached.
* `number`: the maximum age, in milliseconds, of the stale data that can be returned.
* `false`: disables this behavior.
* a function: receives the error response (if any), the current cache entry (in the
  `loading` state, holding the stale data) and the error, and returns one of the values
  above.

::: warning

A response is treated as an error when its status is rejected by axios's
[`validateStatus`](https://axios-http.com/docs/handling_errors). In that case, if
`staleIfError` resolves to `true` (or to a number that still covers the entry), the stale
cache is returned instead of the server's "invalid" response.

To keep the server's response, use a predicate that only allows stale data when there is no
response:

:::

```ts
const customPredicate = (response, cache, error) => {
  // Only returns stale data when there is no response (network errors)
  return !response;

  // Requests with a response still follow axios's default behavior
  // and throw an error, but the error keeps the response
};

axios.get('/api/data', {
  cache: {
    staleIfError: customPredicate
  }
});
```

## cache.override

* Type: `boolean`
* Default: `false`

Bypasses the current cache and always makes a new HTTP request. The current cache entry is
not deleted; it is replaced when the response arrives.

Unlike `cache: { enabled: false }`, this does not disable the cache. It only skips the
checks made before the request, so all post-request options still work as expected. An
overriding request does not wait for concurrent requests to the same key and does not send
`If-None-Match` or `If-Modified-Since` headers.

## cache.vary

* Type: `string[] | boolean`
* Default: `true`

Configures how the HTTP `Vary` header is handled.

* `true`: handles `Vary` automatically (default, recommended).
* `false`: disables `Vary` checks (**WARNING: can cause cache poisoning**).
* `string[]`: uses these request headers instead of the server's `Vary` list. Their values
  are always part of the cache key, whether set globally or per request, even when the
  response has no `Vary` header.

When the server responds with a `Vary` header, the library stores the values of the listed
request headers with the cache entry. A later request with different values for those
headers gets its own cache entry:

```ts
// Request with an Authorization header
await axios.get('/api/users', {
  headers: { authorization: 'Bearer token-A' }
});
// Server responds with: Vary: Authorization
// The entry stores { authorization: 'Bearer token-A' } alongside the response

// Different authorization = different cache entry
await axios.get('/api/users', {
  headers: { authorization: 'Bearer token-B' }
});
// The Authorization value does not match, so this request switches to a
// Vary-aware ID that includes its header value and makes its own request
```

A response with `Vary: *` is stored as stale right away, so every later request revalidates
it with the server.

## cache.hydrate

* Type:
  `undefined | ((cache: CachedStorageValue | StaleStorageValue | LoadingStorageValue) => void | Promise<void>)`
* Default: `undefined`

Called when a network request is needed but an older, probably expired, cache entry exists.
It receives the current cache entry **BEFORE** the network request starts, so you can update
your UI with the old data in the meantime. The request waits for the returned promise, so
keep this function fast.

This avoids *flickering* the UI, especially on slow networks or with a persisted cache in
mobile apps.

::: warning

If the request is answered from a valid cache, no network request is made and `hydrate`
**IS NOT CALLED**, as the axios promise resolves right away. It is also not called for
entries that must be revalidated (`Cache-Control: must-revalidate`).

:::

```ts {7,13}
// Example of a function that renders data on the screen
function render(data) {}

const response = await axios.get(/* [!code focus:10] */ 'url', {
  // Called right away if axios needs to make a network request
  cache: {
    hydrate: (cache) => render(cache.data.data)
  }
});

// After the network request ends, re-render the UI
// with the fresh data
render(response.data);
```

---

---
url: https://axios-cache-interceptor.js.org/config/response-object.md
---
# Response object

Axios Cache Interceptor adds a few cache-related properties to the standard axios response.

## id

* Type: `string`

The [Request ID](../guide/request-id.md) used in this request.

It was either generated by the [key generator](../guide/request-id.md#custom-generator) or
provided through [`config.id`](./request-specifics.md#id).

```ts
const response = await axios.get('url', { id: 'my-overridden-id' });

// This request used 'my-overridden-id' instead of
// the ID the key generator would have produced
response.id === 'my-overridden-id';
```

## cached

* Type: `boolean`

Whether the response data came from the cache (`true`) or from the network (`false`). A
`304 Not Modified` revalidation also returns `true`, because the data comes from the existing
cache entry.

::: tip

This does not tell you whether the request could have been cached. Options such as
[`cache.override`](./request-specifics.md#cache-override) make a network request even when a
cached response exists.

:::

## stale

* Type: `boolean | undefined`

`true` when the response was served from a stale entry, for example when
[`cache.staleIfError`](./request-specifics.md#cache-staleiferror) returned cached data after
a failed request. It is also `true` for requests that waited on a concurrent revalidation of
a stale entry. It is `false` for fresh cache hits and `undefined` for network responses,
including `304` revalidations.
